name: Lecanemab
route_note: Intravenous infusion every two weeks, with every-four-week IV or weekly subcutaneous autoinjector maintenance in the US.
originator: BioArctic (Uppsala University research of Lars Lannfelt) with Eisai

discovery.by: Lars Lannfelt and colleagues, Uppsala University / BioArctic
discovery.note: Derived from the murine antibody mAb158, raised against amyloid-beta protofibrils after study of the 'Arctic' APP mutation; humanised and developed with Eisai.

rx_status: prescription (specialist; amyloid confirmation and MRI monitoring required)
tagline: Anti-amyloid antibody that modestly slows early Alzheimer's disease
summary: Lecanemab is a humanised IgG1 antibody that binds soluble amyloid-beta protofibrils and clears amyloid plaques. In the Clarity AD trial it slowed decline on a clinical dementia scale by about 27% over 18 months in early Alzheimer's disease, at the cost of amyloid-related imaging abnormalities.
mechanism: Lecanemab preferentially binds large soluble amyloid-beta aggregates (protofibrils), considered among the most neurotoxic species, and also binds plaques. Antibody-coated amyloid is cleared by microglial Fc-receptor-mediated phagocytosis, lowering brain amyloid measured by PET.

Amyloid removal can disturb vessel walls containing amyloid (cerebral amyloid angiopathy), producing amyloid-related imaging abnormalities with oedema (ARIA-E) or haemorrhage (ARIA-H). Risk is highest in people homozygous for the APOE ε4 allele.
uses: Mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia due to Alzheimer's disease with confirmed amyloid pathology

history.title: Arctic mutation
history.detail: Uppsala researchers describe the Arctic APP mutation, which increases protofibril formation, inspiring the protofibril-targeting antibody.

history.title: Clarity AD
history.detail: Phase 3 results (van Dyck et al., NEJM) show 27% slower decline on CDR-SB versus placebo at 18 months.

history.title: FDA accelerated approval
history.detail: In January the FDA grants accelerated approval based on amyloid reduction.

history.title: Traditional approval
history.detail: In July the FDA converts to traditional approval with a boxed warning for ARIA; Japan approves later that year.

history.title: UK and China
history.detail: The MHRA approves lecanemab for APOE ε4 non-carriers and heterozygotes; NICE does not recommend it for NHS funding.

history.title: EU approval
history.detail: After an initial negative CHMP opinion and re-examination, the European Commission authorises Leqembi for APOE ε4 non-carriers and heterozygotes.

history.title: Subcutaneous maintenance
history.detail: The FDA approves the Leqembi Iqlik subcutaneous autoinjector for weekly maintenance dosing.

serious: Symptomatic or serious ARIA including seizures
Death associated with brain oedema or haemorrhage
safety.boxed_warning: Amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA), which can be serious and life-threatening; risk is higher in APOE ε4 homozygotes, who should be tested before treatment. Caution with thrombolytics and anticoagulants.

facts: Lecanemab was the first anti-amyloid antibody to receive traditional (full) FDA approval based on clinical benefit.
Its benefit on the 18-point CDR-SB scale in Clarity AD was a 0.45-point difference over 18 months.

references.title: NEJM: Lecanemab in Early Alzheimer's Disease (2023)
